# nonScalar

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a scalar.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonScalar() — Checks whether a value is **not** a scalar. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.4.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonScalar<T>(value: T | string | number | boolean | symbol | bigint): value is T;
```

`nonScalar(value)` is the same test as `!isScalar(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

A primitive that carries a single value: string, number, boolean, symbol or bigint. `null` and `undefined` are primitives too, but they carry no value and do not qualify.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                                   | Description         |
| :-------- | :----------------------------------------------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| string \| number \| boolean \| symbol \| bigint` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a scalar; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonScalar({}); // => true
nonScalar([]); // => true
nonScalar(null); // => true
nonScalar("abc"); // => false
nonScalar(1); // => false
nonScalar(true); // => false
nonScalar(10n); // => false
```
